channel.title: Identity Field Notes
channel.description: AI-driven, source-linked identity security news for practitioners.

item.title: Identity Field Notes: September 23 Recap
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-23. Yesterday’s strongest identity developments centered on an actively exploited OAuth authorization-server flaw, agent governance, identity-graph visibility, AD migration risk, and an emerging agentic SOC model.

item.title: Identity Field Notes: Token Theft, Trust Abuse and Agent Control
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-22. Yesterday’s strongest identity stories centered on OAuth and session-token abuse, privileged Entra persistence, critical-infrastructure credential exposure, and emerging controls for AI-agent identities.

item.title: Identity Field Notes: September 21 Recap
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-21. Yesterday’s strongest identity signals were a hardening passkey deadline, a third-party application-key breach, session theft, and new controls for CI/CD authorization.

item.title: AI-Agent Sandboxes Fail at the Trust Boundary
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-20. Researchers disclosed two OpenAI Codex sandbox escapes that enabled host-level command execution and unauthorized file writes from supposedly constrained agent sessions.

item.title: Identity Recap: Agent Credentials, Edge Injection and IGA-to-PAM
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-17. September 17 brought a sharp warning on exposed AI-agent credentials, a supply-chain compromise rooted in standing cloud privilege, and two vendor moves toward governed agent and privileged access.

item.title: Identity Field Notes — September 17, 2026
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-16. Yesterday’s strongest identity signals were critical Cisco ISE and Keycloak flaws, early evidence of AI-agent reconnaissance, and Google’s expansion of agent authorization into the smart home.

item.title: Identity Field Notes: Token Security Moves From Guidance to Operations
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-15. Yesterday’s strongest identity developments centered on token protection, granular session controls, automated least-privilege remediation, resilient CIAM, and regional identity infrastructure.

item.title: Agent Consent Moves Into the Control Plane
item.description: Highlights from 2026-09-14. AWS introduced a managed OAuth consent and session-binding portal for AI agents, while the queued Okta threat articles were published on earlier dates and are excluded.

item.title: When the Workflow Is the Identity Boundary
item.description: The strongest new signals are not another MFA feature, but evidence that AI workflows and stolen machine credentials are becoming direct authorization paths into enterprise data.

item.title: The identity control plane is getting crowded
item.description: Okta pushes deeper into PAM and IGA, agent administration moves into the IAM control plane, and active cloud intrusions show why MFA alone is not a session-security strategy.

item.title: The service account problem is becoming the agent identity problem
item.description: AI agents are adding speed and autonomy to an identity class most organizations already struggle to inventory and govern.

item.title: Privilege is moving from account-level to action-level
item.description: AI agents are forcing PAM teams to ask a harder question than who got access: what was the identity allowed to do after the session opened?

item.title: Authentication succeeded. That does not mean the session is trustworthy.
item.description: Recent research makes the case for treating session tokens, MFA seed material and post-authentication persistence as privileged assets in their own right.
